messages.subject: Extract Likelihood, Posterior and Probabilities
parts:
Hi Phil,

I looked at the manual and the structure of the output of the mirt function, but I would wish to extract some additional informations:

1. I want to extract the probabilities of all items evaluated at Theta.

2. I want to extract the individual likelihood, namely \prod_i f_i( x_{pi} |  \theta ), the evaluated likelihood of all response patterns at every grid point theta (in Theta).

3. I want to extract the computed posterior of each response pattern.

Is it possible to get this information from "standard output"?

Many thanks and kind regards,
Alexander

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Extract Likelihood, Posterior and Probabilities
parts:
Hi Alexander,

I think an earlier post on this forum will help you with these tasks: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/mirt-package/OAWxlSwqPzQ. The point just requires including the normed density of θ into the computations and summing across the grid in 2). It's also available in standard mirt objects under the @Pl slot, Hope that helps.

Phil

On Fri, Aug 8, 2014 at 11:16 AM, <a.rob...@bifie.at> wrote:

Thank you. But admittedly I read the mentioned post and this solution is not really something what I had in mind.

I think it just requires a bit of tweaking to make it work over a grid of θ values for each response pattern, but the idea is the same. 
 

Recently I recognized the "customPriorFun" argument in mirt/technical. This looks very promising. Do you an example how to apply this argument?

Sure. Below is how to implement a truncated uniform prior (truncated above and below |3|).

> library(mirt)
> 
> myprior <- function(Theta){
+     #truncated uniform prior (unidimensional only)
+     prior <- dunif(Theta[,1], min = -3, max=3)
+     return(prior / sum(prior))
+ }
> 
> dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
> mod <- mirt(dat, 1) #standard Gaussian distribution
Iteration: 29, Log-Lik: -2658.805, Max-Change: 0.00010
> mod2 <- mirt(dat, 1, technical = list(customPriorFun = myprior)) #truncated uniform
Iteration: 15, Log-Lik: -2660.030, Max-Change: 0.00005
> 
> mod

Call:
mirt(data = dat, model = 1)

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 29 EM iterations.
M-step optimizer used: BFGS 
Number of rectangular quadrature used: 41

Log-likelihood = -2658.805
AIC = 5337.61; AICc = 5337.833
BIC = 5386.688; SABIC = 5354.927
G2 (21) = 31.7, p = 0.0628
RMSEA = 0.023, CFI = 0.939, TLI = 0.924
> mod2

Call:
mirt(data = dat, model = 1, technical = list(customPriorFun = myprior))

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 15 EM iterations.
M-step optimizer used: BFGS 
Number of rectangular quadrature used: 41

Log-likelihood = -2660.03
AIC = 5340.06; AICc = 5340.282
BIC = 5389.137; SABIC = 5357.377
G2 (21) = 34.15, p = 0.0349
RMSEA = 0.025, CFI = 0.925, TLI = 0.907

Many thanks in advance and kind regards,
Alexander

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Extract Likelihood, Posterior and Probabilities
parts:
Okay this has been added on the dev version. The function from the previous example now needs to be defined with an 'Etable' argument to work, even if it isn't used. Like so:  

> myprior <- function(Theta, Etable){

+     #truncated uniform prior (unidimensional only)
+     prior <- dunif(Theta[,1], min = -3, max=3)
+     return(prior / sum(prior))
+ }

Note that on the first run the Etable will be NULL since the prior must be set first before the Etable can be defined (same issue with the empirical histogram, in which case the default is just to use a standard Gaussian distribution for the first E-step). Just add a condition if(is.null(Etable)){} else{} statement to deal with this issue if you plan to use the Etable. Thanks for the suggestion.



Phil
